problem_text: A coalition of five workers uses the exact same model family and exact same model revision, but each worker receives a different role-specific prompt. Does that coalition constitute five independent evidentiary sources for validating a scientific or mathematical claim?
expected_epistemic_core: Different prompts can create search or reasoning diversity.
Shared model/revision creates common lineage and correlated failure modes.
Five executions therefore must not automatically be counted as five independent evidentiary sources.
Independence requires materially distinct evidence, method, data, model lineage, or external reproduction depending on the claim.

workers.role_task: Specify the decision rule for when multiple workers may be counted as independent evidence.
Audit which dependencies are shared and which would have to differ to support evidentiary independence.
Construct a concrete failure case showing why five same-lineage outputs can agree and still all be wrong.
Produce a checkpoint-ready rule preserving both useful prompt diversity and the independence limitation.
Formalize execution diversity versus evidentiary independence using explicit variables or logical conditions.
